A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same tree-Wasserstein method and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Reported task revisions are identifiable and do not prevent comparison of the documents.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original synthetic, classification, runtime, and ablation experiments, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: Original experiments are retained, and Appendix E.3.6 adds cosine-cost WMD/GMD and direct-distance classification results.

M1.justification: The multi-scale hyperbolic diffusion embedding, HD-LCA construction, binary tree decoding, and TWD formula remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures; expanded assumptions and experimental descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The datasets remain, including MNIST, but Appendix D.1 and Table 2 redefine both biological classification targets: Zeisel changes from 7 cell types to 47 subclasses, and CBMC from 13 types to 56 subclasses. These finer targets materially change the reported task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds direct Euclidean and cosine feature-space classification baselines. Existing TWD, WMD/GMD, and ED/OT-ED comparators remain. Changes from names ending in '-TW' to '-TWD' are renamings.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 now reports divisive biclustering to generate classification subclasses, replacing the previously stated cell-type labels. Appendix E.3.6 also introduces cosine-ground-cost WMD/GMD evaluations and direct-distance controls. The 70/30 splits and kNN settings remain; the PDFs do not establish whether the relabeled cell experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3.6 examines whether baseline ground-metric choice and classification without Wasserstein transport explain performance differences. This extends the existing initial-metric ablation; earlier tree-construction, embedding, curvature, noise, and non-hierarchical-data analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run evaluations and mean/standard-deviation results. The added tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure appears.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add numerical results, including cosine-cost WMD at 93.5±0.3 on CLASSIC and GMD at 86.9±0.5 on Zeisel. Retained tables and plots preserve their values, including v1 Table 5 becoming v2 Table 7. Unchanged cell scores cannot establish equivalent performance under the revised classification targets.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and their proofs replace explicit 1/sqrt(2) and 1 bounds with unspecified positive constants. Section 4.1 introduces a complete, simply connected, negatively curved manifold formulation, and Section 4.4 explicitly conditions recovery on heat-kernel convergence. Theorem C.1 is also restated using d_T^(2alpha), materially revising the formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of latent-feature-hierarchy recovery, novel tree decoding, efficient computation, and classification advantages. The introduction's Wasserstein-versus-TWD wording reflects the existing identity for tree ground metrics.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of density normalization under nonuniform sampling, the distinction between initial and transport ground metrics, and single-linkage suitability in hyperbolic space. Appendix E.3.6 interprets the new controls as supporting hierarchy learning, but its broad superiority statement overlooks Table 1's CLASSIC exception: WMD scores 97.2 versus 96.9 for the proposed method.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds explicit Word2Vec/Gene2Vec setup information, identifies Google News pretraining, supplies embedding/data access links, and specifies baseline ground metrics and subclass construction. Hardware, hyperparameter grids, selected settings, and the diffusion-landmark implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting manifold assumptions and diffusion normalization, plus Fakcharoenphol et al. (2003) in the new single-linkage discussion, and removes Luecken and Theis (2019). Positioning against Euclidean-ground-metric TWD methods is elaborated while the central novelty distinction remains.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction, problem formulation, and related-work discussion are rewritten; Appendix D.1 expands, and E.3.6 and F.5 are added. Diffusion-convergence discussion moves into Appendix A.2. The overall organization and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5–6, renumbers the previous Table 5 as Table 7, and relocates existing appendix displays. Figure 2 updates comparator labels, Algorithms 1–2 use more compact formatting, and Table 1's caption expands. Existing empirical plots retain their graphical data.

improvement.justification: The added ground-metric controls and direct-distance baselines address specific gaps in evaluating the empirical advantage, while clearer assumptions and data provenance improve transparency. The gain is limited: quantitative guarantees become weaker, revised cell labels accompany unexplained identical scores, and Appendix E.3.6 overgeneralizes superiority despite the retained CLASSIC WMD exception.
